subject: Authorization failures + fallback routing — confirmation & credit request

From: Anika Shah <anika.shah@nimbus-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
Cc: ops@nimbus-payments.com
Date: Fri, 08 Jan 2027 03:20:00 +0000
Subject: Service disruption impacting authorization calls — urgent

Jordan —

We're seeing a large spike in 503/504s coming from Redwood for our /v1/authorize endpoint in ap-southeast-1 this morning. First observed ~03:10 UTC; errors and high tail latency continued until about 03:40 UTC. This caused a batch of authorizations to queue and some timeouts on our side, which impacted settlement for a handful of merchants.

Attached is a short pcap extract and a sample of request IDs from our side (pcap_sample_0308.txt). Please confirm:
- Whether this window is visible from Redwood's telemetry and what the root cause was
- Whether this counts as an availability SLO hit for apac and how credit eligibility will be assessed
- A timeline for an official post-incident report and any immediate mitigations we should apply

We need confirmation of the exact downtime window and the list of affected endpoints for our compliance team (SOC-2 evidence request).

Thanks,
Anika Shah
Sr. Platform Ops
Nimbus Payments

Anika — thanks for the heads up and for the pcap. I'm escalating this to our incidents team and copying Evelyn and Karthik who own SLOs and the apac serving fabric.

Can you please also send:
- A compact list of request IDs and timestamps (UTC) for failed requests (we can match these to token-level traces)
- Any CloudFront/edge IDs you see in the request headers (helps tie routing)

We will pull token-level traces and the regional autoscaler logs and confirm the exact window. At first glance your timestamps are consistent with an auth proxy error pattern we saw in a separate alert.

I'll follow up within 2 business hours with preliminary confirmation and whether this meets our SLA credit threshold. If needed we'll provide an interim credit calculation and a full postmortem.

-Jordan

Date: Sat, 09 Jan 2027 10:15:00 +0000
Subject: Preliminary confirmation — ap-southeast-1 auth routing fallback and SLO impact

Hi Anika —

Appreciate the quick report and the pcap. We've pulled regional traces and autoscaler events for the time range you flagged (03:05–03:50 UTC). Preliminary findings: 

- Between 03:09:42 and 03:37:18 UTC we observed elevated 5xxs and 95th/99th latency on the authorization path in ap-southeast-1.
- Root cause (prelim): an expired TLS cert that affected a subset of the auth proxy fleet, which triggered our routing controller to evacuate traffic to a warm pool. The warm pool contained instances with cold KV caches and different kernel options which increased per-token latency and caused some upstream timeouts.
- This behavior created a de facto availability degradation for certain tenant routing buckets (including Nimbus Payments' edge IDs you supplied).

SLA/credit posture: based on our initial calculations this meets the threshold for a partial availability credit for the region during the confirmed window. We're attaching an estimated credit calculation and the logs bundle for your compliance team. Final credit determination and amount will be confirmed after the postmortem and full log reconciliation.

Next steps we are taking:
- Deliver a full post-incident report by EOD 2027-01-13 (root cause, sequence of events, remediation, and steps to prevent recurrence)
- Provide token-level traces for the exact request IDs you share (please send them when convenient)
- Offer a temporary pro-rata credit estimate now and finalize after reconciliation

Attachments included: logs_bundle_20270108.tar.gz, sla_calc_nimbus_20270109.xlsx

We understand SOC-2 timelines — if you need a signed evidence packet for auditors sooner, tell us the exact items required and we'll prioritize.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
